title: Sharp Honest Expected Length for a Paired Binary Causal Contrast at Crossover
banked_reason: reaching field tier on the sharp-crossover object requires a new full-model decision-theoretic characterization, rather than completion of an identified bounded missing lemma.
gap_reasons: The requested Stat deliverable is a uniform all-budget minimax risk/expected-length order with a single data-only honest interval, but the core delivers only restricted-family lower support and recasts the frontier and construction as open pointwise questions.

Its approximate-minimizer existence result is explicitly nonconstructive, so it is not an evaluator-ready estimator/interval and cannot supply the stated data-only honest interval or a Stat frontier-advance theorem.

The related-work discussion gives no theorem-level comparison for several listed weak-overlap and empirical-Bernstein sources, and the unnamed companion predecessor is neither identified nor compared precisely enough to establish what nonduplicative contribution remains.
proof_attempt_summary: The original all-budget risk and adaptive-interval frontier was rejected as duplicating the predecessor kernel, so discovery investigated the sharp honest-length crossover. Two solve rounds established restricted-family information and testing support, but the full-model limiting value, sharp lower bound, and evaluator-ready attaining interval remain open. Math review passed; the independent terminal validity gate confirmed incremental contribution below the field floor, and no Lean formalization was launched.
tldr: This note records the sharp pointwise crossover question for full-model honest expected length of a predeclared paired binary causal contrast. Proved support verifies legal four-cell endpoints with a common assignment scale and nonzero feasible boundary contrasts, computes exact observed-product affinity, and gives a pair-adaptive finite-sample two-law expected-length lower bound. Spline refinement exhausts only the declared continuous restricted family; a control-coupling witness rules out full-model density. Abstract approximate minimizing honest intervals exist nonconstructively. Sharp limiting values, convergence, full-model least-favorability, the exact modulus-to-length relation and an explicit data-evaluable attaining interval remain unresolved. The companion predecessor supplies the all-budget order frontier and adaptive interval as background only. Connors et al. motivate a paired survival/resource-use question with binary resource use fixed in advance; no dataset-applicability claim is made.
gap: The credited rate-frontier benchmark leaves the sharp normalized honest-length criterion \(\mathcal H_n(\rho_n(t))/a_n\) unresolved. Gaussian interval and between-class-modulus results motivate the question but do not determine its answer for the maintained full paired-binary law class.
fill: The explicit spline modulus supplies an evaluable lower-program handle using legal binary cells, own-law boundary envelopes and exact product affinity. The open task is to determine both normalized limit values and derive a matching full-parent-class honest interval, including any obstruction from the restricted lower-program family. No completed sharp theorem or clinical-precision claim is made.
